discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms entangled via Rydberg blockade, for quantum simulation and quantum computing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned single atoms, held in optical tweezers, into a controllable quantum platform. Saffman, working with Walker, and Browaeys, working with Grangier, gave the first demonstrations of the Rydberg blockade between two individual atoms, and they used it to entangle neutral atoms and to realise quantum gates. Browaeys then built defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms in arbitrary geometries. With these arrays he made exact quantum simulations of interacting spin models. Lukin's group developed the same approach. They observed quantum phase transitions and many-body scars, and they recently demonstrated logical qubits and error-corrected circuits on atom arrays. This work combines exquisite control of individual quantum systems with entanglement on a large scale. It is a central achievement of the second quantum revolution: foundational ideas about single particles and entanglement have become an operational tool for exploring many-body physics and for quantum computation.
